subtype_info: Plasmodium falciparum malaria complicated by secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and pancytopenia
title: Pancytopenia with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in Plasmodium falciparum: A unusual presentation
case_text:
There was another 11-year-old male child admitted to pediatrics emergency with the complaint of fever (15 days), red color urine, black terry color stool, and nasal bleeding past 3 days for whom peripheral smear for Pf malaria came out to be positive. Hematological as well other laboratory parameters were suggestive as HLH and child respond to anti-malarial therapy.
In both cases, sHLH is the cause of pancytopenia. After anti-malarial therapy, both children responded very well and hematological parameters starting to improve within a week of therapy [Table 1]. All these cases are in regular follow-up and till the last follow-up at 6 weeks of discharge there both children were doing well and were hematological parameters also improved.

     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Malaria
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: Plasmodium falciparum malaria complicated by secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and pancytopenia
